effective.basis: Old state: UDE official card rulings (Sangan/Witch: 'If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify', captured 2005-06-16) through Konami's own per-set rulings documents - Machina Mayhem (2010-04-06, 18 days before the Edison snapshot), Starstrike Blast (2010-11-16), Storm of Ragnarok (2011-02-02). New state: KDE-US Tournament Policy section 'Card/Hand/Deck Verification' forbids verifying the opponent's Deck (first located capture 2019-04-03; still current in v2.5, 2025-09-05). No dated announcement of the change was found, so the interval 2011-02-02 .. 2019-04-03 stays open.

corroboration.title: UDE official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings (capture 2005-06-16, inside the GOAT window)
corroboration.quote: You must show your opponent the monster you select from your Deck for this card's effect. If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify.

corroboration.title: Konami, Machina Mayhem Structure Deck Card Rulings, compiled April 6th 2010 (18 days before the Edison snapshot)
corroboration.quote: If you do not have "Commander Covington" in your Deck, your opponent can ask to verify.

corroboration.title: Konami, Storm of Ragnarok Card Rulings, compiled February 2 2011 - the latest positive attestation of the old state
corroboration.quote: If there is no longer a monster in your hand that you can Special Summon when this effect resolves, your opponent may briefly verify that this is the case.

changes.historical_text: When this card is sent to the Graveyard as a result of battle, you can Special Summon 1 LIGHT monster with an ATK of 1500 or less in face-up Attack Position from your Deck. Then shuffle your Deck.
changes.summary: Period procedure plus a relaxed activation condition, not a text erratum: the GOAT script keeps only the free-Monster-Zone test in s.target (the modern Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard over LOCATION_DECK is removed), so the battle-destruction trigger can be used with no LIGHT monster of 1500 or less ATK left in the Deck, and it proves the failed search by revealing the Deck (Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_DECK)); the modern script requires a valid target to activate and never reveals.

review.notes: Chain starts at v1 (DB1-EN052, 2004-10-12), the text the GOAT variant carries exactly. Every later revision is cosmetic ('as a result of battle' -> 'by battle' -> 'destroyed by battle and sent to the Graveyard', dropped shuffle wording, PSCT colon, GY); v0's parenthetical '(no Tribute is required for monsters of Level 5 or more)' predates the baseline and states a Special Summon property that is true regardless. Note the lineage is not monotonic: v4 (SRL-088 in Legendary Collection, 2010-10-01) reprints the older v1 wording after v2/v3 had already modernised it. Packet observation: modern_text_matches_version reports index 3, but the modern cdb text is character-identical to v5 (YS11-EN013) and differs from v3 by a colon and a comma - the matcher appears to normalise punctuation and returns the first hit. It does not affect this record, which carries no modern_text_version. Flagged chronology-unresolved because the script encodes both era components and only the reveal is dated: the 2005-06-16 UDE capture and the 2008-12-15 Card FAQ capture both give this card the standard recruiter rulings with no verification or activation sentence, exactly as for Mystic Tomato and Giant Rat, so the end date of its relaxed activation condition is unattested. The general verification procedure does cover recruiters - KDE's own modern policy uses a failed Mystic Tomato search as its example of what may no longer be verified.
